read: full: abstract and introduction (pp. 1-2), definition system (pp. 2-3), dataset design (pp. 3-4), evaluation (pp. 4-6), experiments and results (pp. 6-9), conclusion and limitations (p. 9); appendices A (prompt construction) and B (human evaluation) read (pp. 12-13); remaining appendices skimmed
venue_now: arXiv preprint 2407.15240v6, 31 Mar 2025 (p. 1); no venue shown in the text
what_it_is: BIGbench (Biases of Image Generation benchmark) measures social bias in text-to-image models (pp. 1-2). Its 47,040 prompts are built in three parts. Identity prompts combine acquired attributes (179 occupations in 15 categories, social relations, adjective pairs) with protected attributes (sex, race, age). GPT-4o wrote supplement prompts, which were screened by hand, and photorealism prompts were assigned at random (pp. 3-4, 12). A fine-tuned InternVL-4B aligner labels the sex, race and age of people in the generated images. From those labels the paper reports implicit and explicit bias scores and a 'manifestation factor' for eight text-to-image models and three debiasing methods (pp. 4-7).
domain: text-to-image generation: social bias (occupations, social relations, characteristics against sex, race and age)
size: 47,040 prompts; 8 images per prompt per model; 8 text-to-image models and 3 debiasing methods (pp. 1, 6)
source_of_items: generated from attribute lists: identity prompts combined from attribute lists, supplement prompts written by GPT-4o and screened by hand, photorealism prompts assigned at random (pp. 3-4, 12)
instances: generated: a fixed prompt set built combinatorially from attribute lists, with randomly assigned prompt parts (pp. 3, 12)
has_gold_traces: no: the ground truth is demographic proportions (UN and US BLS statistics) and the attributes named in each prompt (p. 4)
evaluation: automated multimodal-LLM aligner (fine-tuned Mini-InternVL-4B 1.5) that labels protected attributes in generated images; cosine-similarity implicit bias score, explicit bias score (share of correctly generated images) and manifestation factor (pp. 4-6)
human_validation: Ten trained annotators of different races labelled 1,000 generated images (majority vote, with a second round of voting and discussion when votes were close) as ground truth for the aligner; the fine-tuned InternVL reaches 97.93% average alignment accuracy (sex 100, race 98.6, age 95.2) (pp. 6, 13)
contamination_measures: none (not applicable: it evaluates image generators)

engtrace_use.sentence: S-E1 (L182-190): 'Generalist suites like MMLU (Hendrycks et al., 2021a), BIG-Bench (Luo et al., 2024), and SuperGPQA (Du et al., 2025) restrict assessment to factual recall via multiple-choice questions, ...'
engtrace_use.explanation: The citation points at the wrong paper. The sentence names the generalist language-model suite BIG-Bench, but this entry is 'BIGbench', a benchmark of social bias in text-to-image models (title and abstract, p. 1). It has no multiple-choice questions, tests no factual recall and evaluates no language model: it scores the demographic make-up of generated images with an MLLM aligner (pp. 4-6). The only link to the sentence is the near-identical name.

suggested_wording: None for EngTrace: the paper has no bearing on its related work. If it were ever cited, an accurate clause would be: 'BIGbench (Luo et al., 2024) measures social bias in text-to-image models over 47,040 prompts.'
facts_to_cite: a benchmark of social biases in text-to-image models, not a language-model suite (title and abstract, p. 1)
47,040 prompts built from occupation, social-relation and characteristic attributes combined with sex, race and age (pp. 1, 3-4)
evaluates 8 text-to-image models and 3 debiasing methods with a fine-tuned MLLM aligner validated on 1,000 human-labelled images (pp. 1, 6, 13)
overlap_with_engtrace: None that matters. It differs in modality (image generation), task (social bias) and measurement (demographic proportions); it has no engineering content, no gold traces and no step-level evaluation. The only shared trait is building prompts combinatorially from attribute lists.
